newsitem.title: USA: U.S. oil, gas producers raise drilling budgets.
newsitem.headline: U.S. oil, gas producers raise drilling budgets.

text.p: Most U.S. oil and natural gas producers expect to increase exploration and production spending in 1997, accounting firm Arthur Andersen said in its annual industry survey released on Tuesday.
Seven in ten companies in the survey said they planned to boost domestic exploration and production spending, up from about four in ten in the year-ago survey that said they planned to hike spending.
Two-thirds of the companies surveyed, including 81 percent of the majors and large independents, said they expected a shortage of U.S. offshore drilling rigs next year.
One in three producers surveyed also predicted a disruption in natural gas supplies during the coming winter heating season.
The companies surveyed forecast a median wellhead West Texas Intermediate crude oil price of $20.00 a barrel in 1997 and 1998, rising to $22.50 in 2001.
The survey respondents forecast a median spot wellhead price for Gulf Coast natural gas of $2.10 per thousand cubic feet (mcf) in 1997, rising to $2.30 mcf in 2001, the firm said.
